input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 on its own meets the preferred position: Customer may terminate for convenience on thirty days' notice with a refund of prepaid Fees, and Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a committed term. However, Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights," which conflicts with and could be read to override Section 9.4, leaving us locked into a multi-year spend with no effective convenience exit (the walk-away position). There is no order-of-precedence clause to resolve the conflict. The minimal fix is to make the Section 2.1 minimum expressly subject to our termination rights and reduce it pro rata on termination, leaving Section 9.4 intact.

ops.oldText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: on a take-or-pay basis. This commitment is subject to Customer's termination and reduction rights under this Agreement, including Section 9.4, and the annual minimum will be reduced pro rata for any Services terminated or reduced in accordance with those rights.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We conformed the three-year take-or-pay minimum to our termination rights so it cannot override the 30-day convenience termination and pro-rata refund we agreed in Section 9.4. Our playbook requires a customer convenience exit without penalty in any multi-year term; if helpful, we can instead cap the exposure on early exit at three months' fees.
proposal.summary: Make the § 2.1 take-or-pay commitment subject to Customer's § 9.4 convenience termination, with pro-rata reduction of the minimum.
